s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of unilateral weakness and vomiting with headache
salient_findings: Right ankle clonus and upgoing plantar response
key_facts: 36-year-old man of Indian origin
Presented at 2:30 a.m. with acute symptoms
Awoke around midnight with headache and vomiting
No visual change or speech disturbance
Odd sensations and occasional tremors in right arm and leg over prior two weeks
Nonsmoker, denied alcohol or drug use
Worked as a teacher
Pulse was 88 bpm, blood pressure 124/87 mmHg, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air
Alert with intact speech
Partial left ptosis
Equal reactive pupils, no ophthalmoplegia
Motor strength 0/5 in right upper limb, 3/5 proximally and 2/5 distally in right lower limb
Brisk reflexes bilaterally with right ankle clonus
NIH Stroke Scale score was 7
Noncontrast CT of the head showed no acute pathology
Incidental 4 × 6 mm hyperdense focus in left parasagittal frontal cortex suggestive of cavernoma

shortlist.label: Ischemic stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Recent ischemic infarction in the left paramedian medulla on brain MRI

shortlist.label: Cavernous malformation
shortlist.why_kept: Incidental 4 × 6 mm hyperdense focus in left parasagittal frontal cortex suggestive of cavernoma on noncontrast CT of the head

shortlist.label: Brainstem stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of unilateral weakness and vomiting with headache, and brain MRI showing recent ischemic infarction in the left paramedian medulla

shortlist.label: Lateral medullary syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms, including partial left ptosis, bilateral torsional nystagmus, and right-sided weakness, are consistent with this syndrome

shortlist.label: Central nervous system vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, this diagnosis cannot be entirely ruled out without further testing, given the patient's acute presentation and lack of other clear explanations

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including acute right-sided weakness, numbness, and brisk reflexes with right ankle clonus, along with the brain MRI showing a recent ischemic infarction in the left paramedian medulla, are consistent with a brainstem stroke.

rejected.label: Ischemic stroke
rejected.why: While the patient had an ischemic infarction, the specific location in the brainstem and the constellation of symptoms point more specifically to a brainstem stroke.

rejected.label: Cavernous malformation
rejected.why: The incidental finding of a cavernoma in the left parasagittal frontal cortex does not directly explain the patient's acute symptoms.

rejected.label: Lateral medullary syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms do not perfectly match the classic presentation of lateral medullary syndrome, which typically includes dysphagia, hoarseness, and nystagmus, among other symptoms.

rejected.label: Central nervous system vasculitis
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of inflammation or vasculitis in the patient's presentation or diagnostic tests.
